youtube_title: Lake Station, Indiana: Liverpool, Lake County's lost first county seat (Lake Station request)
youtube:
You asked for Lake Station! Lake County's first county seat was Liverpool, and it vanished. It was laid out in 1836 where Deep River meets the Little Calumet, and in three days buyers paid $16,000 for lots. In 1839 it became the county seat and work began on a courthouse, but settlers protested, and in 1840 the seat moved to Lake Court House, soon renamed Crown Point. Historian T. H. Ball wrote that the unfinished courthouse was floated downriver on a scow to Blue Island, Illinois; others dispute that story. George Earle, who had pushed for Liverpool, went on to found Hobart, and in 1852 he laid out Lake Station. Liverpool emptied, and fire took what was left. Its site lies in today's Lake Station and New Chicago, and only the name survives. Comment your town, and it could be next! #LakeStation #NewChicago #LakeCounty #Indiana #History #LaPorteAfterDark #Shorts

All pictures are drawn. Narration is a computer voice. Sources: John O. Bowers, 'Dream Cities of the Calumet' (Lake County Historical Association, 1929); T. H. Ball, Northwestern Indiana from 1800 to 1900 (1900); both transcribed at inportercounty.org; Lowell Public Library (Richard Schmal, Lowell Tribune, 1994); Crown Point Community Library; Town of New Chicago; South Shore Convention and Visitors Authority; Encyclopedia of Chicago. More LaPorte County history: https://laporteweathernow.com/history
